description: 186n-Downburst_Transmission_Tower is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Amal Elawady, Florida International University (fiu.edu). Transmission Line Systems (TLSs) serve as the primary infrastructure for delivering electricity from power plants to residential buildings, healthcare facilities, and industrial zones. The extensive network of electricity transmission towers and power lines spans approximately 640,000 miles across the United States, ensuring nationwide electricity distribution. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: Hurricane, downburst winds,  transmission tower,  transmission line systems,  aeroelastic testing. Published 2024-12-02. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
